ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a symmetrical dual-power-supply voltage regulator circuit. The three-terminal regulator in the upper branch is labeled CW7812, and the three-terminal regulator in the lower branch is labeled CW7912; the middle terminals of the two are connected to the central common node. The input voltage Ut on the left is applied between the upper and lower input terminals, marked upper positive and lower negative; the upper end of the output terminal on the right is marked "+", the lower end is marked "-", and the output voltage Uo is measured from the upper positive output terminal to the lower negative output terminal. The figure also has filtering/bypass capacitors such as C1, C2, C3, C4, C5 connected. Reasoning: The problem gives Ut = 32 V and the input voltage is normal, therefore the two fixed regulators work in the regulated state. CW7812 outputs +12 V relative to the common node, and CW7912 outputs -12 V relative to the common node. Therefore the voltage between the upper and lower output terminals on the right is +12 V - (-12 V) = 24 V.
